column3: NASB follows the critical text without “immediately”; “ministering” is rendered “waited on.”
NASB renders “they knew Him” as “they knew who He was.”
NASB supplies “Jesus” and “left the house”; “very early in the night” is rendered “in the early morning, while it was still dark.”
NASB renders “the neighboring villages” as “the towns nearby” and “I have come forth” as “I came for.”
NASB follows the critical text (“went into their synagogues”).
NASB supplies “Jesus” and has “falling on his knees before Him,” including “before Him” from the Textus Receptus.
NASB follows the reading “moved with compassion”; a few manuscripts read “being angry,” so the meaning is uncertain.
NASB has no “as He spoke,” like the critical text.
NASB supplies “Jesus” and renders “much” as “freely,” “the matter” as “the news,” and “solitary places” as “unpopulated areas.”
